brief: A seven-cell honeycomb work surface, covered on top, with every open outside edge finished with caps.

requirements.requirement: Seven-cell honeycomb work surface (one central hex plus six surrounding, all connected)
requirements.evidence: 7 pieces at center 0,0,0 and its six neighbors (-1,0; -1,1; 0,-1; 0,1; 1,-1; 1,0) forming compact honeycomb, joined with 6 jointBolts on center cell to clear LOOSE_BODY.
7 top covers: cover:-1,0,0;full;top, cover:-1,1,0;full;top, cover:0,-1,0;full;top, cover:0,0,0;full;top, cover:0,1,0;full;top, cover:1,-1,0;full;top, cover:1,0,0;full;top – one per cell.

requirements.requirement: Every open outside edge finished with caps
requirements.evidence: 18 caps placed on all 18 perimeter slots (3 per outer cell): e.g., cap:-1,0,0;*;90/150/210 etc. covering all open edges; check_build meshClash clear, no open cap sockets remaining.

finish.summary: Built seven-cell honeycomb at level 0, added full top cover to each cell for continuous work surface, and capped all 18 exterior edges (3 caps per outer hex). Verified with check_build: ok true, meshClash clear, no issues.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
